text:
We checked “4 auto size error” and found 2 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 1 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Text frame has no paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: text frames “gfdgfdfgfghfg”, “fgdfgd”, “dfsdffdgd” (page 1)
• Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

2. Auto-size text frame set up incorrectly
Frontify grows auto-size frames as people type, and can’t match how these settings resize the frame.
Where: text frames “gfdgfdfgfghfg” (page 1, turn on No Line Breaks), “fgdfgd” (page 1, Only width, height, and WidthAndHeight are supported), “dfsdffdgd” (page 1, turn on No Line Breaks)
• For each frame, open Object > Text Frame Options > Auto-Size and make the change noted next to it.
Learn more

May change how it looks

3. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: the paragraph style “[Basic Paragraph]”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
